Reported at Pure Country Convenience Store.

A supercell moved southeast across Live Oak County into Bee County. This storm produced a 5 to 10 mile swath of damage mainly due to high winds. A couple of semi-trucks were turned over along Interstate 37. Several power poles were snapped or leaned over along with highway signs …
Quarter to golfball size hail reported at Three Rivers Federal Prison.

Large trees were uprooted in Largarto. Patio furtiture was also blown downwind.
Public report of estimated gust from 60 to 65 mph on the west side of Lake Corpus Christi near the Lagarto Store.
Large trees were blown down. A deer blind was destroyed.
Trees were blown down and into the roadway along Farm to Market Road 2049.

Trees were blown down and into the roadway on Farm to Market Road 534.
Trees were blown down and into the roadway on Farm to Market Road 888.
Spotters reported a tornado briefly touched down to the south-southeast of Whitsett.

Storm chasers observed a brief tornado just south of Whitsett. The tornado damaged large trees and a mobile home and uprooted a hay shed. This damage was observed just east of Highway 281 about a half of a mile southeast of Whitsett.
Storm Chasers observed a brief rope tornado on the ground for about 1 minute in an open field. No damage was observed.
Spotters reported a tornado briefly touched down south of Nell.
Storm chasers observed a brief tornado southwest of Three Rivers just south of Farm to Market Road 1042. The tornado touched down in an open field. No damage was observed.
Spotter reported large hail that ranged from golf ball to baseball size.
Nickel sized hail occurred near George West.
Quarter sized hail was reported at a grocery store in George West.
Spotter estimated 65 mph winds to the southeast of Clegg.
Quarter sized hail was reported southeast of Clegg.
Storm chasers and spotters observed a tornado south of Clegg. The tornado touched down over open ranch country. No damage was observed.
Damage occurred to sheds and feeders on a ranch near the intersection of Highway 59 and Farm to Market Road 624.
Half dollar sized hail occurred in Clegg.
Several residents reported a tornado briefly touching down southwest of Lagarto. No damage was reported.
Nickel sized hail occurred on Interstate 37 near Whitsett along with winds estimated to be near 50 mph.
Winds broke tree limbs of 6-8 inches in diameter near the community of Whitsett.
A large tree was blown down on Oakville Road in Three Rivers.
A large tree was blown down near the intersection of Farm to Market Road 2049 and County Road 243 north of the community of Ray Point.
Coop observer reported quarter sized hail.
COOP observer reported multiple downed tree limbs.
Spotter reported quarter sized hail occurred in the southwest portion of Three Rivers.
Quarter sized hail occurred near the merger of Interstate 37 and Highway 281.
Police officer reported golf ball sized hail near County Road 403 off of Highway 72 west of Three Rivers.
Spotter reported three large trees blown down.
Quarter sized hail was reported east of Dinero.
Trees were blown near Lagarto. Power lines were blown down into the roads. A back porch was blown off of a residence.
Quarter sized hail occurred on Interstate 37 and Highway 59 interchange.
Quarter sized hail occurred near Highway 72 southeast of Choke Canyon Reservoir. Report was relayed by San Antonio broadcast media.
Public posted pictures to social media of quarter sized hail in Three Rivers.
Second thunderstorm produced quarter sized hail in Three Rivers.

Around a dozen power poles and several highway signs were blown down along Interstate 37 near Oakville. A few roofs were peeled back on buildings in Oakville. Several trees and sheds were blown down also.
Weak waterspout over northeast part of Choke Canyon Reservoir moved onshore.
Live Oak County Sheriff's Office reported a waterspout over Lake Corpus Christi near Pernitas Point.
Several trees were blown down across the city of Three Rivers. An abandoned building collapsed. The Boys and Girls Club building received roof damage.
Two power poles were blown down just north of George West.
Public sent pictures of quarter sized hail near Clegg.
Public reported quarter sized hail near Swinney Switch through social media.
Public reported golf ball sized hail near Swinney Switch.
Public reported quarter sized hail northeast of Swinney Switch through social media.
RV park estimated wind gusts up to 60 mph.
A tin roof was blown off of a building and severed power lines.

An isolated area of damage occurred with a tornado near Pernitas Point. A tree was uprooted along with damage to two stop signs in the neighborhood. Maximum wind speed was estimated at 80 mph.
Power poles were broken at the ground on Highway 99.
A tree limb 12 inches in diameter was broken near observer's home.
Tree limbs and power lines were blown down between Interstate 37 and Esseville.
Observer estimated wind gusts up to 65 mph.
Sporadic tree damage from thunderstorm winds was reported throughout much of Live Oak County.
Public report of tree branches blown down.
RAWS site GWRT2 in George West reported a wind gust to 60 mph.
Observer reported nickel sized hail in Whitsett.
Storm chaser reported quarter sized hail near Anna Rose.
Public reported quarter sized hail to the west-southwest of George West. Radar indicated much larger hail occurred to the southwest of this report.
Law enforcement reported pea to nickel sized hail occurred at the intersection of Farm to Market Roads 534 and 3162.

An EF-0 tornado with 85 mph winds touched down just east of Highway 281 on County Road 151 and moved southwest along the county road. The tornado snapped large branches and split a few trees. The tornado lifted just west of Highway 281.
A strong storm with a definite hail core produced quarter size hail across the city of Three Rivers for a couple minutes according to the public.
Social media photos of quarter size hail from Dinero, TX to Swinney Switch, TX. Time estimated from radar.
DPS Reported half-dollar sized (1.25) hail at intersection if I-37 and FM 99, near Whitsett.
Live Oak County EMC confirmed minor tree and porch damage along a narrow path through George West. Media relayed photo of well developed funnel cloud with this storm.
Trees down were reported in the city.
Reports were received of a tree blocking the road.
